candidates.title: DAGent: Evaluate-then-Grow Planning for Deep Research Agents
candidates.citationVelocity: published 2 days ago; Semantic Scholar 429 rate-limited, no citation data obtainable this round
credibilityEvidence: Table 1 main results across BrowseComp-Plus/GAIA/xbench-DeepSearch, 4 backbones + GPT-5 extension
Appendix F explicit, scoped Limitations section
5 baseline agent families (ReAct, Summary, Fold, Flash-Searcher, FlowSearch)
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Full ablation and baseline tables across 3 benchmarks and multiple backbones support the core planning claim; RL extension (DAGRPO) only validated at small scale (1 backbone, 3 seeds, 21 steps)
reproducibilityEvidence: RL training recipe disclosed but only run at small scale
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Scoped claim (incremental planning beats Plan-then-Patch on the 3 tested benchmarks) is well supported by baseline/ablation tables and cross-backbone replication
candidates.primaryLimitation: RL trained only on Qwen3-8B with LoRA, 21 steps, 3 seeds; structural-compliance-to-accuracy link is correlational per the paper's own wording
candidates.presentationReason: Method, baselines, and limitations are clearly delineated with explicit appendix sections
candidates.reason: Strongest credibility signal of today's pool: only peer-reviewed (NeurIPS 2026) candidate found, with open code and the most complete baseline/ablation coverage; directly addresses a core, currently debated design question (DAG multi-agent planning) for deep research products.

candidates.title: TomasuLLM: Out-of-Order Speculative Execution for LLM Agents
candidates.citationVelocity: published 10 days ago; Semantic Scholar 429 rate-limited, no citation data obtainable this round
candidates.institution: HKUST (majority); co-authors from Nanjing University, KAUST, Zhejiang Lab
communitySignals: not found on HF Daily Papers or Papers with Code
credibilityEvidence: 3 benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified 100 tasks, Terminal-Bench 2.0 28 tasks, SWE-Marathon 18 sessions)
4,010 audited commit-validation records, zero false accepts
explicit measured-vs-replay-estimate distinction in sensitivity analysis (Figure 14)
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Multi-benchmark results plus ablation/sensitivity analysis with honest disclosure of which points are measured vs. trace-replay estimated; sample sizes (100/28/18 tasks) are modest
reproducibilityEvidence: Built on open-source Pi harness v0.84.2, but no code release link found for TomasuLLM's own runtime
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Scoped claim supportable given correctness audit and multi-benchmark speedups, but small sample sizes and reliance on some replay-estimated numbers limit confidence to extrapolate
candidates.primaryLimitation: Small task counts per benchmark (100/28/18); some sandbox-concurrency speedup numbers (16/32 slots) are trace-replay estimates, not measured re-runs, limited by E2B account's 8-slot cap
candidates.presentationReason: Mechanism (operand rule, drafters, commit validation) and measured-vs-estimated distinction are clearly explained
candidates.reason: Concrete, quantified latency fix for a widely-felt coding-agent pain point (idling on long tool calls), with a rigorous correctness-validation design (4,010 zero-false-accept audit); selected for 應用/系統效能 angle alongside DAGent's 方法 angle and Prompted Identity's 評測/侵限 angle.

candidates.title: Prompted Identity Degrades Cooperation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
candidates.citationVelocity: published 4 days ago; Semantic Scholar 429 rate-limited, no citation data obtainable this round
communitySignals: not found on HF Daily Papers or Papers with Code
credibilityEvidence: Unlabeled permutation baseline + shuffled/mislabeled causal control isolating label effect from capability differences
AMI statistic with 95% bootstrap CIs, 50 runs per configuration
Cross-validated with ground-truth GPQA-Diamond benchmark beyond the custom-designed games
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Controlled causal manipulation (label shuffling) plus GLM regression ruling out roster-size confound and cross-task replication support the core claim; scope limited to custom games due to no existing benchmark fitting the no-individual-incentive requirement
reproducibilityEvidence: No code or dataset release link found in the paper
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Scoped claim (identity labels, independent of capability, drive cooperation cost in the tested games/benchmark) is well supported by the causal shuffle-label control
candidates.primaryLimitation: Tested only with up to 5 open-weight model families, text-only, custom-designed cooperative games; larger rosters, closed models, and real agentic workflows untested
candidates.presentationReason: Section 5 Limitations explicitly scopes the claims; experimental design (unlabeled/labeled/mislabeled) is clearly laid out
candidates.reason: Novel, rigorously-controlled finding with immediate practical relevance to the fast-growing pattern of multi-provider multi-agent systems; provides the 評測/極限 angle this trio needed alongside two 方法/系統 papers.
